takeaway: ControlNet keeps Stable Diffusion locked and attaches a trainable copy of its encoder and middle block; the copy reads the condition image (an edge map) and adds its outputs back into the U-Net's skip connections and middle block through zero-initialised convolutions.

reader_questions.glance: Which part is new and trainable, which part is frozen, and where does the condition image enter?
reader_questions.detail: How does the trainable copy connect to the locked U-Net (zero convolutions into the 12 skips and the middle block), and what goes into the copy (z_t plus the encoded condition c_f)?

concepts.name: Locked U-Net over its trainable copy
concepts.takes: Composition of T2I-Adapter Fig. 3: the frozen Stable Diffusion in one cool panel across the top (snowflake), the trainable branch underneath in a warm accent (flame), the real condition image entering at the bottom-left, and vertical links rising from the branch into circled + glyphs on the U-Net. From animate-anyone-2023-fig2: the second network drawn with the same silhouette as the first, directly beneath it, so 'copy' reads without text.
concepts.sketch: Top row: z_t slab -> SD encoder trapezoid -> middle -> (+) -> decoder trapezoid -> eps slab, under a bracket 'Stable Diffusion (locked)'; skip from the encoder to the decoder through a (+) under the encoder. Second row in the warm accent: (+) -> encoder copy (same trapezoid, directly under the original) -> middle copy, named 'ControlNet (trainable copy)'; 'zero conv' labels on the straight links up into the two (+). Condition column at the left: Canny edge map -> E -> zero conv -> (+) with z_t. No containers: the locked/trainable split is carried by tone, the bracket and the name, as in dreampose-2023-fig2.

concepts.name: Twin hourglasses, one link per resolution
concepts.takes: Animate Anyone Fig. 2: two stacked hourglass silhouettes with bars per block and one straight vertical link per block from the upper network into the lower; inputs as real images on the left.
concepts.sketch: SD hourglass with bars for the 4 resolutions (64, 32, 16, 8) and the middle; ControlNet half-hourglass below with 4+1 bars; one zero-conv link per resolution into the skip at that level.

concepts.name: Vertical stack with side skips
concepts.takes: DiT Fig. 3 (kb card): the backbone stacked in a narrow column, skip paths as elbow lines down one side merging through circled +, the conditioning branch as a parallel column beside it.
concepts.sketch: SD column bottom-to-top (z_t at the base, eps at the top), skip elbow on its right; ControlNet column further right with zero-conv taps leftwards into the (+).

why: A puts the reader's three questions in three places: locked model on top, trainable copy directly under it in the accent colour with the same trapezoid (so 'clone' is visible), and the condition image entering at the bottom-left. Collapsing the 12 repeated encoder blocks into one trapezoid per network keeps the main line to 6 units, which a single 3.28 in column can print legibly. B shows the 4 resolutions but needs 5 links and 4 nested skip arcs that the links must cross, too dense for a single column; C makes the figure tall and puts the condition image far from the copy that reads it.
highlight: ControlNet's parts are the only warm (orange, bold) nodes, named 'ControlNet (trainable copy)'; the encoder copy repeats the locked encoder's trapezoid directly beneath it; each link back into the locked network is a straight arrow labelled 'zero conv' into a circled +. Stable Diffusion stays cool and muted under a 'Stable Diffusion (locked)' bracket.
